questions.question: What is the core job of BLIP-3's vision token sampler?
options: Compress encoded image views into a bounded token sequence the language model can consume
Generate final text without a language model
Replace the image encoder with OCR rules
Encrypt every image patch before inference
questions.explanation: The sampler bridges modalities by reducing many visual features to a manageable sequence while trying to preserve task-relevant evidence.

questions.question: How does BLIP-3 simplify the BLIP-2 training design?
options: It replaces the Q-Former with a Perceiver-style sampler and uses one autoregressive text-token objective
It removes the language model and trains only a vision encoder
It uses separate language models for every patch
It trains only on single-image classification labels
questions.explanation: The paper highlights both changes: a more scalable sampler and one autoregressive objective across training stages.

questions.question: Two images each use four detail patches plus one global view. At 128 query tokens per view, how many visual tokens are modeled?
questions.explanation: Each image has five encoded views. Two images times five views times 128 query tokens equals 1,280 visual tokens.

questions.question: What did the paper's Stage-2 high-resolution ablation show?
options: OCR improved while aggregate general VQA remained roughly stable
Every benchmark doubled
OCR fell because patches were forbidden
The language model was no longer needed
questions.explanation: At the largest tested grid, aggregate OCR rose from 64.6 to 67.2 while general VQA stayed close to the Stage-1 baseline.

questions.question: Why mix some single-image examples into the multi-image instruction-tuning stage?
options: To reduce degradation of previously learned single-image capability
To make image order irrelevant
To eliminate the need for evaluation
To convert the model into an image generator
questions.explanation: The paper explicitly reuses a subset of single-image data while teaching interleaved multi-image behavior.

questions.question: A product must compare several images in order. Which evidence should most strongly influence checkpoint choice?
options: Multi-image curriculum fit and representative cross-image evaluation
The longest model name
A single aggregate caption score
Whether the images share a file extension
questions.explanation: Parameter count alone does not teach interleaved behavior. The training curriculum and task-specific cross-image tests address the actual contract.

questions.question: What should a team do before deploying a model card example that uses trust_remote_code=True?
options: Inspect and pin the repository code and revision, then evaluate the exact dependency set
Assume remote code cannot execute locally
Disable all model version pinning
Use benchmark scores as a security review
questions.explanation: Remote model code is executable code. Treat it as a dependency: inspect it, pin it, and test the exact version you will operate.
